title: FLLAC students’ 48-hour strike after 13 March protest
reason: Provisional event-type exclusion only: opened coverage confirms a 48-hour work stoppage and restates the student demands, but does not describe a public gathering or attendance. Retained pending_evidence; do not treat a strike announcement/work stoppage by itself as a qualifying mass gathering.
notes: Potential continuation of the 13 March FLLAC protest is unresolved because the same faculty and demands appear in the March 20 strike reports, but a distinct public assembly on 20–21 March is not documented. Do not merge the work stoppage into E001.
open_questions: Did a public assembly accompany the 20–21 March strike?
Is this a follow-up campaign action to E001, and did it involve a new gathering?

title: Public-school teachers’ strike and unspecified student/union protests around 20–21 March
reason: Provisional event-type/threshold exclusion: ITUC-Africa describes teachers arrested during on-site strike action and says unspecified protests by students and unions helped secure releases, but gives no public-gathering form, site, time or attendance. Retained pending_evidence, not a definitive exclusion.
notes: ITUC-Africa reports 14 teachers were arrested at Collège d’enseignement général L’Entente in Cotonou on 21 March while observing the strike and released after protests from pupils and unions; it separately reports teacher and union-official arrests on 20–21 March in Cotonou and Abomey. The source’s unspecified plural “protests” cannot establish a qualifying 50-person gathering. No strike count is treated as protest attendance.
open_questions: Did students or union members assemble publicly in response, at what site and when?
Did any one gathering include at least 50 simultaneous participants?
What were the precise demands directed to the state and any state response to a gathering?
